definitions.gloss: dog and monkey; (figuratively) two parties who get along badly
definitions.explanation: Literally "dog and monkey," animals proverbially said to fight on sight. Used almost exclusively in the idiom {犬猿|けんえん}の{仲|なか} to describe two people on extremely bad terms.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}は{犬猿|けんえん}の{仲|なか}だ。
examples.english: The two of them are bitter enemies.

examples.japanese: {兄弟|きょうだい}なのに{犬猿|けんえん}の{仲|なか}で、ほとんど{話|はな}さない。
examples.english: Although they are brothers, they are on terrible terms and hardly speak.

examples.japanese: かつては{犬猿|けんえん}の{仲|なか}だった{両国|りょうこく}も、{今|いま}では{協力|きょうりょく}し{合|あ}っている。
examples.english: The two countries, once bitter rivals, now cooperate with each other.

notes:
Almost always appears in the set phrase {犬猿|けんえん}の{仲|なか} ("on dog-and-monkey terms"), describing people who cannot get along. Rarely used alone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {犬猿|けんえん}の{仲|なか}: bitter enemies; on very bad terms
- {犬猿|けんえん}の{仲|なか}になる: to become bitter enemies

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {不仲|ふなか}: discord — plain description of a poor relationship, without the vivid imagery
